Court No. - 84

Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 5441 of 2023
Applicant :- Laltesh
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Applicant :- Punya Sheel Pandey Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Vinay Kumar Tripathi Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
1. Criminal Misc. Exemption Application is allowed.
2. Supplementary affidavit on behalf of the applicant and the counter affidavit on behalf of complainant filed today are taken on record.

3. This application has been moved on behalf of the applicant Laltesh seeking anticipatory bail in Complaint Case No. 480 of 2020, under Sections 376, 384, 120-B, 506 IPC, Police Station Kotwali,
District Mathura.

4. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the informant as well as the learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
5.

It has been argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has apprehension of his arrest in the above-mentioned case, whereas there is no credible evidence against him.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.

It is further submitted that when the police investigated the matter on the basis of F.I.R. lodged on the basis of same set of facts, final Laltesh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188164539/
1 report was submitted, as no evidence was collected against the applicant.

sentences.text: It is a case based on criminal complaint.
Two real brothers have been alleged to have committed rape upon the prosecutrix, which is not probable.
It is also submitted that there was some money dispute between the parties and due to this reason, the present prosecution has been started.
It has been submitted that in case applicant is granted anticipatory bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and would obey all conditions of bail.

6. Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and submitted that cogent and sufficient evidence was adduced before the trial court under Sections 200 and 202 CrPC on the basis of which summoning order was passed and the applicant was summoned to face trial in this case.
It is further submitted that it is a case where a young prosecutrix was raped by the applicant and other co-accused and she was blackmailed also.

7. In this matter, it has been alleged against the applicant that on 5.6.2016 at about 8.00 p.m. the present applicant alongwith co-accused Manoj by administering some intoxicant to the prosecutrix committed rape against her and obtained some obscene photographs.
Applicant alongwith other co-accused person also blackmailed the prosecutrix on the basis of said photographs and she was also threatened to make the aforesaid photographs viral on social media.

F.I.R. was lodged but after investigation final report was submitted and protest petition was filed which was treated as complaint and following the procedure of complaint case, the applicant was summoned to face trial for the offence under Sections 376, 384, 120-B, 506 IPC.

8. In Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1, the Hon'ble Apex Court has settled the controversy finally by holding the anticipatory bail need not be of limited duration invariably.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In appropriate case, it can continue upto conclusion of trial.
9. It has been further held therein that anticipatory bail granted can, depending on the conduct and behavior of the accused, continue after filing of the charge sheet till end of trial.

10. It has been further held by the Hon'ble Apex Court that while considering an application for grant of anticipatory bail, the court has to consider the nature of the offence, the role of the person,
the likelihood of his influencing the course of investigation, or tampering with evidence including intimidating witnesses, likelihood of fleeing justice, such as leaving the country, etc.

It has further been held that Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail, or refuse it.
Whether to grant or not is a matter of discretion.

11. Hence, considering the settled principles of law regarding anticipatory bail, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant, all attending facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that allegations are serious in nature, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, in my view, it is not a fit case for anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Prayer made in the application is refused.
12. The application is rejected.
